podcast.body: This single, released on June 5th, 1964, was the first record to feature David Bowie, marking the beginning of his recorded music career. He was later influenced by Lou Reed. "First record to feature him was a single called Liza Jane."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Book of World Records Version 1.0 - Part 2

podcast.body: This song marked David Bowie's (then David Jones) first ever appearance on record, released on June 5, 1964, with the group David Jones and the King Bees. It was an early attempt by Bowie to make a mark in the music industry. "The first time David Bowie ever appeared on record, the song is Liza Jane."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This was David Jones's (later David Bowie) first-ever single, released in June 1964 with his group, The King Bees. "Earlier that year, June 1964, David had released his first-ever single."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This was the only single released under the moniker Davy Jones with The King Bees, marking the first recording to feature David Robert Jones. Despite being promoted by major label Decca Records, the single sold poorly, leading Jones to leave the band after a few weeks. "This is Liza Jane, the only single released under the moniker, Davy Jones with the King Bees."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
